UnitStatement: AGENTS.md maps the general Chirality agent framework onto Chirality App development without redefining the canonical agent framework.
The file specifies how the existing agent roles should be used for this project.
Executable prompts and TASK briefs must derive paths from the active checkout.
Resolve REPO_ROOT with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
Set WORKING_ROOT to {REPO_ROOT}/projects/chirality-app-dev.
Use {REPO_ROOT} and {WORKING_ROOT} in project-local instructions and briefs instead of machine-specific absolute paths.
Normative agents define runtime contracts, product boundaries, validation policy, and agent workflow constraints.
Operative agents execute bounded app-integration tranches, implementation slices, tests, evidence updates, and docs updates.
Evaluative agents review, reconcile, audit, and decide whether outputs are acceptable for the next stage.
WORKING_ITEMS (type 1) is the primary parent for bounded app-integration tranches; it selects scope, integrates results, validates, updates coordination state, and prepares closeout.
TASK (type 2) executes one sealed implementation, assessment, docs, or evidence sub-scope with explicit read/write bounds.
CHANGE (type 1) performs final Git/file-state closeout for validated tranches: scoped status review, staging, commit, and fast-forward-safe push.
RECONCILIATION (type 1) detects cross-surface conflicts, stale assumptions, dependency issues, and inconsistent terminology.
REVIEW (type 1) reviews project outputs against scope, validation evidence, product boundaries, and acceptance criteria.
RESEARCH (type 1) performs evidence-grounded, read-only inquiry over accepted decompositions, governance/source docs, and retrieval indexes, returning cited findings without changing project state.
AUDIT_* (type 2) runs bounded checks for governance conformance, dependency closure, release-quality evidence, and epistemic integrity.
Bounded app-integration tranches are the default execution unit.
A parent WORKING_ITEMS agent may orchestrate parallel TASK fan-out only when subscopes are separable, briefs are explicit, and write scopes are disjoint.
Agents may write inside the selected tranche scope, required evidence and coordination artifacts, and project-local plans created under the issue-plan rule.
Agents must not write root governance files, root agent instructions, root skills, or root tools unless the human explicitly directs that governance work.

Other agents may be working in the monorepo with disjoint write scopes; treat unrelated dirty files outside the selected tranche scope as external state and do not fix, stage, revert, or interpret them unless the human directs that work.
When a tranche is complete, validated, and closeout rules allow, the parent WORKING_ITEMS agent hands off to a CHANGE agent/subagent for final Git/file-state review.
CHANGE should commit and push the validated tranche as the ordinary terminal action when git state allows closeout.
Per-run APPROVE: tokens are not required for scoped closeout commit/push.
If a CHANGE agent/subagent is unavailable, perform the CHANGE closeout checklist inline.
CHANGE closeout checklist: inspect root git status.
CHANGE closeout checklist: confirm validation evidence and skipped-check notes.
CHANGE closeout checklist: stage only files in the selected tranche write scope, required evidence/coordination artifacts, and any explicitly created governance-issue plan.
CHANGE closeout checklist: do not stage unrelated dirty files.
CHANGE closeout checklist: commit the scoped tranche when validation and staging are clean.
CHANGE closeout checklist: fetch or otherwise verify upstream state before pushing.
CHANGE closeout checklist: push only when the upstream branch can be fast-forwarded to the local scoped commit.
If the remote branch has advanced and local HEAD does not already include it, stop and surface the conflict; do not merge, rebase, force push, or judge another agent's work during ordinary closeout.
Git closeout is source-control hygiene; it is not lifecycle issuance, release readiness, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance acceptance.

If concrete, actionable issues that would improve the agentic development loop, project governance, agents, or skills are discovered, record them in at most one timestamped plan under {WORKING_ROOT}/plans/ for the session.
Do not create a plan merely to satisfy the issue-plan rule when no actionable issue was found.
